photograph.identityScope: Hans Hillewaert labels a Southern North Sea pea crab. Preparation, sex and live material properties are not independently documented in the caption. A soft adult female form uses separate anatomical evidence; the selected photograph cannot calibrate living translucency or internal organs.

sources.title: Smithsonian Contributions to Zoology306 · selected Pinnotheres pisum account
sources.scope: Selected complete P.pisum species account on PDF page9 was read by text extraction: nominal synonyms, eastern Atlantic/Mediterranean occurrence and bivalve association. The subsequent adult-female description concerns P.tellinae and is explicitly not transferred to P.pisum. Body outline is compared with the separately licensed real P.pisum photograph; no measured anatomy or feeding mechanics imported.

sources.title: Naturalis — North Sea crustaceans: Pinnotheres pisum
sources.scope: Institutional morphology read: soft translucent female versus hard male, small eyes, smooth equal chelae and short curved walking dactyli roughly half the propodus. Third-maxilliped distinction is recorded, but detailed palp diagnosis is not yet reconstructed/validated. Naturalis female/male size ordering is retained over a conflicting reversed ordering in the Habitas summary.

sources.title: D.Atkins1958 — British Pea-crabs (Pinnotheres)
sources.scope: Publisher abstract/preview only: sexual/stage differences in shell and swimming hairs. Full letter unavailable in this access. No male swimming or host mechanism assigned to the selected soft female study.

retrieval.accessMethod: Publisher abstract/preview; not subscription full text

sources.title: Raymond B.Manning1993 — West African pinnotherid crabs, comparative Pinnotheres diagnosis
sources.scope: Selected printed126 actual Figure1b/text and key130 read: P.pisum has a long spatulate third-maxilliped propodus and shorter basal styliform dactylus. Only this explicitly captioned P.pisum comparison is used; West African new taxa/stages are not assigned to this species. Small authored palp cues added; no measured complete mouthpart mechanics.

retrieval.accessMethod: PDF selected actual page2/printed126 rendered/read; selected key text read

shape.before: The earlier withheld oval/rod-limbed draft is preserved on the body sheet.
shape.changed: A selected soft adult female study now has a continuously rounded inflated envelope, inconspicuous small eyes, short eight-legged articulation, strongly curved short dactyli, equal small chelae and a broad female ventral cover. Small separate third-maxilliped propodus/dactylus cues replace bead-like mouthparts.
shape.remaining: Soft-body deformation, setal filtering structures, gonopores, gills, host fit and complete third-maxilliped anatomy are incomplete. The selected model is unmeasured and still simplified. Translucency is an illustration, without calibrated scattering, visible organs or a physiological claim. The source photo does not independently determine sex or preparation.

sourceAssessment: Naturalis morphology was directly read, Atkins1958 publisher abstract/preview was scoped separately, and Manning1993 actual printed126 Figure1b/text was rendered/read for P.pisum comparative mouthparts. The longer spatulate propodus and shorter basal styliform dactylus are distinguished from related pea-crab genera. The Hans Hillewaert Southern North Sea photograph was viewed. No male swimming assigned to the selected soft-female study.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Replaced a flat-rimmed shell with one continuous rounded envelope after frontal comparison.
Reduced exposed eye stalks and antennule length; shortened curved terminal limbs.
Added separately scoped simple P.pisum maxilliped cues after viewing the captioned primary comparison.
